note: Coaches per train, by DMRC line code. The animation draws every train on a line with this many coaches.

sources.LN3 LN4: DMRC press release, 8 Nov 2022 ('DMRC introduces 8-coach trains on its Red Line from today'): the conversion of all 6-coach trains to 8-coach on the Blue Line (Line-3/4, Dwarka Sec-21 to Noida Electronic City/Vaishali) was completed the year before.
sources.LN1: Same release: Red Line 6-to-8 conversion 'likely to be completed by 2024'; DMRC release of 25 Dec 2024: TS-01 'expanded ... to 8 coaches in 2023'. Wikipedia (Red Line): all converted by April 2024.
sources.LN2: Same 8 Nov 2022 release: 'the conversion of all 6-coach trains into 8-coach trains on the Yellow Line' was completed the year before.
sources.LN7 LN7EXTN: DMRC release of 30 Oct 2026: Pink Line occupancy displays show coaches C1 to C6. Release of 15 Nov 2024: 90 coaches (15 trains) for the Pink Line extension.
sources.LN8 LN8EXTN: DMRC release of 15 Nov 2024: 144 coaches (24 trains) for the Magenta Line extension.
sources.LN10: Wikipedia (Airport Express Line): eight six-car CAF trains.
sources.LN11: Wikipedia (Rapid Metro Gurgaon): trains operate in three-car configurations.
sources.LN5 LN6 LN9: Assumed. The 8 Nov 2022 release says standard-gauge lines take up to 6 coaches and the fleet then had 22 four-coach trains, without naming their line. Wikipedia: Green and Violet stock was ordered mostly as 4-car trains (46 of 48); Grey uses the Pink/Magenta stock. Green is taken as 4, Violet and Grey as 6.
sources.third_rail LN11: Wikipedia (Rapid Metro Gurgaon): 'powered by a 750-volt direct current (DC) traction system supplied through a third rail'. Every other line is drawn with 25 kV overhead wires.
